title: Lamb Tagine with Apricots and Almonds
subtitle: Moroccan slow-braised lamb with dried fruit and spices
excerpt: Shoulder of lamb braised slowly with warming spices, preserved lemon, dried apricots, and almonds until the meat is fall-apart tender. Served over couscous.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tagine refers both to the conical earthenware cooking vessel and the slow-cooked stew made in it. The Moroccan tradition of combining meat with dried fruit and warm spices is ancient, with origins in the medieval Persian and Arab culinary traditions that spread across North Africa with the expansion of Islam. Sweet and savoury combinations are central to Moroccan cooking: honey and preserved lemon balance the warm spice blends (ras el hanout, cumin, coriander). Lamb shoulder is the ideal cut: it has enough fat and collagen to remain moist through the long braise.

recipeTools.notes: A wide casserole or actual tagine dish.

content.text: Lamb shoulder cut into chunks works better than leg: it has more fat, stays moist during the long braise, and becomes more tender. Brown the lamb in batches over high heat before braising: this deepens the colour and flavour of the sauce. The spices go in with the onion rather than with the meat, so they bloom in oil and do not burn. The tagine needs at least 1.5 to 2 hours to fully tenderise the meat.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wide casserole over high heat. Season the lamb and brown in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until coloured on all sides. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining oil. Cook the onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, ras el hanout, cumin, and cinnamon. Stir for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.

Return the lamb to the casserole. Add the stock, apricots, preserved lemon, and honey. Season. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the lamb is very tender. Stir occasionally, adding a splash of water if it looks dry.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter with toasted almonds and fresh coriander. Serve over couscous.
